notes: Kc values: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Allen, Pereira, Raes & Smith 1998), Table 12. Where Table 12 gives a range, the midpoint is used and the range is kept in kc_range. Where Kc ini is only given at crop-group level, the group value is used.

Stage lengths: FAO-56 Table 11, one representative row per crop (region and planting month recorded in stage_row). Only the PROPORTIONS are used: they are scaled to the local season length from the GGCMI Phase 3 calendar.

Heat thresholds are daily-maximum temperature indicators taken from the cited studies. Schlenker & Roberts (2009) estimate thresholds from within-day temperature exposure; counting days with Tmax above the threshold is a simpler proxy.
Values were transcribed from FAO-56 and the cited papers; check them against the originals before citing this file.

cassava.stage_row: Cassava year 1, rainy season, tropical regions

potato.kc_range: ini 0.50 (roots and tubers group); mid 1.15; end 0.75

rapeseed.stage_row: No Table 11 row; water need not computed

rye.kc_range: Not listed as a grain crop in Table 12; water need not computed

references.fao56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998) Crop evapotranspiration: guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. Rome: FAO.
references.schlenker2009: Schlenker, W. & Roberts, M.J. (2009) Nonlinear temperature effects indicate severe damages to U.S. crop yields under climate change. PNAS 106(37), 15594-15598.
references.yoshida1981: Yoshida, S. (1981) Fundamentals of Rice Crop Science. Los Banos: IRRI. (Spikelet sterility with temperatures above about 35 C at anthesis.)
references.lobell2012: Lobell, D.B., Sibley, A. & Ortiz-Monasterio, J.I. (2012) Extreme heat effects on wheat senescence in India. Nature Climate Change 2, 186-189. (Uses 34 C.)
references.fao33: Doorenbos, J. & Kassam, A.H. (1979) Yield response to water. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 33. Rome: FAO.
references.usda_scs: USDA Soil Conservation Service effective-rainfall method as implemented in FAO CROPWAT: Peff = P(125 - 0.2P)/125 for P <= 250 mm/month; Peff = 125 + 0.1P otherwise.
